dataClassifications.rationale: Raw imagery is large, highly sensitive, and not needed off-device once features are extracted.
Low-sensitivity geometric summary already stripped of raw pixels; local use only, cheap to keep plaintext.
Derived feature vector can re-identify what the drone observed; encrypt before it leaves the device.
Only the aggregate (mean/sum across drones) is useful centrally — CKKS lets the server compute it without seeing inputs.
Operationally necessary, low sensitivity, needed quickly and cheaply for fleet health dashboards.
GPS trace over a restricted site is sensitive on its own, independent of any other signal.
Safety-critical control loop; must never depend on network or cryptographic availability.

manifest.knownVulnerabilities: Not scanned by this generator. Run `npm run security:sbom` to produce results/sbom.json (CycloneDX, via @cyclonedx/cyclonedx-npm) and feed it to a vulnerability scanner (e.g. `npm audit`, Grype, OSV-Scanner) for an actual vulnerability register entry.
manifest.updateMechanism: None implemented. This is a research prototype distributed as source; there is no signed-update or OTA mechanism. A production system would need one before any CRA security-update-policy claim could be supported.
manifest.networkInterfaces: None opened by default. apps/fleet/compare.ts simulates the fleet/aggregator network path in-process (no sockets) so that reported latency/bandwidth numbers are pure compute+serialization cost, not this host's network stack.
manifest.testStatus: See results/ for the latest tools/bench and apps/fleet run artifacts; no automated CI is configured in this prototype.

attackSurface.description: None. No server/socket is opened by any script in this repo.

8 scripts runnable via `npx tsx`/npm scripts (apps/demo/killer-demo.ts, apps/fleet/compare.ts, apps/redteam/intercept-demo.ts, tools/bench/ckks-bench.ts, tools/bench/kernel-bench.ts, tools/bench/util.ts, …). Attack surface here is local-process only: whoever can execute Node in this checkout.
Benchmark/demo/security tools read package.json and package-lock.json and write JSON/CSV under results/. No path comes from untrusted/network input.

node-seal (runtime) and its WASM binary are the actual cryptographic trust base; a compromised upstream package is this prototype's largest realistic attack surface. See results/sbom.json for the full transitive tree.

vulnReport.tool: npm audit (via this repo's own package-lock.json)
